title: Lecture #36: Cranial Nerves V, VII-XII
summary:
# Lecture #36: Cranial Nerves V, VII, VIII, IX, X, XI, XII

**Lecturer:** I. Kurtzer, Ph.D.
**Session:** Lecture #36

## CN V - Trigeminal (Slides 8-13)

### Divisions & Function
*   **V1 (Ophthalmic):** Somatosensation (forehead, eye).
*   **V2 (Maxillary):** Somatosensation (cheek, upper lip).
*   **V3 (Mandibular):** Somatosensation + Motor (jaw, lower face).

### Nuclei (Location: Pons)
*   **Trigeminal Pontine:** Touch & proprioception (face).
*   **Trigeminal Spinal:** Pain & temperature (face). Fibers descend.
*   **Trigeminal Mesencephalic:** Jaw proprioception (unique: 1st order afferents in CNS).
*   **Trigeminal Motor:** Muscles of mastication (V3).

:::correlate
**Trigeminal Neuralgia ("Suicide Disease")**
*   **Mechanism:** Compression of sensory root (often by superior cerebellar artery) → Demyelination.
*   **Presentation:** Sudden, severe pain to eyes, lips, head (100s/day).
*   **Key Feature:** Extreme, debilitating pain.
:::

## CN VII - Facial (Slides 14-20)

### Nuclei (Location: Caudal Pons - Facial Colliculus)
*   **Facial Motor:** Facial expression muscles, Stapedius (middle ear).
*   **Superior Salivatory:** Lacrimal glands (tears), Submandibular/Sublingual glands (saliva).
*   **Gustatory (Solitary):** Taste (anterior 2/3 tongue).
*   **Trigeminal:** Ear somatosensation.

### Upper vs Lower Motor Neuron Lesions
*   **UMN Lesion (Cortical):** **Contralateral** lower face paralysis. Forehead spared (bilateral innervation).
*   **LMN Lesion (CN VII):** **Ipsilateral** entire face paralysis (forehead + lower face).

:::correlate
**Bell's Palsy**
*   **Presentation:** Ipsilateral complete facial paralysis (forehead + lower face).
*   **Associated:** Diminished taste, dry eye (cannot close eye), hyperacusis (stapedius paralysis).
*   **Cause:** CN VII vulnerable in middle ear (idiopathic inflammation, often viral).
:::

## CN VIII - Vestibulocochlear (Slides 21-24)

### Nuclei (Location: Pons/Medulla Junction)
*   **Cochlear:** Hearing (Organ of Corti).
*   **Vestibular:** Head motion/orientation (Semicircular canals, Utricle, Saccule).

:::correlate
**Meniere's Disease**
*   **Triad:** Diminished audition (high frequencies), Aural fullness, Vertigo.
*   **Mechanism:** Inflammation of semicircular canals.
:::

## CN IX - Glossopharyngeal (Slides 25-30)

### Nuclei (Location: Rostral Medulla)
*   **Nucleus Ambiguus:** Stylopharyngeus (swallowing - pharyngeal phase).
*   **Inferior Salivatory:** Parotid gland secretion.
*   **Gustatory (Solitary):** Taste (posterior 1/3 tongue).
*   **Solitary:** Baroreceptor feedback (carotid sinus & body).
*   **Trigeminal:** Posterior 1/3 tongue, throat, ear somatosensation.

## CN X - Vagus (Slides 31-34)

### Nuclei (Location: Rostral Medulla)
:::highyield
**Nucleus Ambiguus:** Striated muscle of soft palate, pharynx (gag reflex), larynx (vocal cords).
**Dorsal Motor Nucleus:** Parasympathetic "Rest & Digest" (↓ HR, ↑ GI secretions/motility).
**Solitary:** Visceral sensory (larynx, esophagus, trachea, thoracic/abdominal viscera, aortic arch chemoreceptors).
**Trigeminal:** Ear/ear canal somatosensation.
:::

**Critical Fact:** Vagus is the **largest autonomic conduit** from brainstem. 65-80% of fibers are **afferent** (sensory).

### Clinical
*   **Unilateral Medulla Lesion:** **Ipsilateral** paralysis (Nucleus Ambiguus).
*   **Unilateral Cortical Lesion:** Largely compensated (bilateral UMN control).

## CN XI - Spinal Accessory (Slides 36-40)

*   **Function:** Somatic motor.
*   **Innervation:** Sternocleidomastoid (SCM), Upper trapezius.
*   **Unique:** Originates in **spinal cord** (C1-C5), ascends through **foramen magnum**, exits via jugular foramen.

:::correlate
**Trapezius Palsy**
*   **Presentation:** Shoulder drooping, Winged scapula.
*   **Causes:** Trauma to posterior cervical triangle, Iatrogenic (lymph node biopsy).
:::

## CN XII - Hypoglossal (Slides 41-44)

*   **Function:** Somatic motor.
*   **Innervation:** All internal + most external tongue muscles.
*   **Clinical:** **Tongue deviates to weak side** (unopposed contralateral genioglossus).

## Medullary Syndromes (Slides 45-46)

:::correlate
**Medial Medullary Syndrome (Anterior Spinal Artery)**
*   **Pyramid (CST):** Contralateral hemiparesis (body).
*   **Medial Lemniscus:** Contralateral tactile/proprioceptive loss (body).
*   **Hypoglossal Nucleus:** Tongue deviates **ipsilateral** (to lesion side).
:::

:::correlate
**Lateral Medullary Syndrome (PICA - Wallenberg Syndrome)**
*   **Spinothalamic Tract:** Contralateral pain/temp loss (body).
*   **Spinotrigeminal Nucleus:** Ipsilateral pain/temp loss (face).
*   **Nucleus Ambiguus:** Hoarseness, dysphagia.
*   **Vestibular Nucleus:** Falling to ipsilateral side.
*   **Inferior Cerebellar Peduncle:** Ipsilateral limb incoordination.
:::
mindmap:
## Cranial Nerves V, VII-XII
### CN V (Trigeminal)
*   **Motor**: Jaw muscles (V3)
*   **Sensory**: Face (Pontine=touch, Spinal=pain/temp)
*   **Trigeminal Neuralgia**: SCA compression
### CN VII (Facial)
*   **Motor**: Facial expression
*   **Parasympathetic**: Tears, Saliva
*   **Sensory**: Taste (ant 2/3 tongue)
*   **Bell's Palsy**: Complete ipsilateral paralysis
### CN VIII (Vestibulocochlear)
*   **Cochlear**: Hearing
*   **Vestibular**: Balance, Vertigo
*   **Meniere's**: Audition+Fullness+Vertigo
### CN IX (Glossopharyngeal)
*   **Swallowing**: Stylopharyngeus
*   **Taste**: Post 1/3 tongue
*   **Baroreceptors**: Carotid sinus
### CN X (Vagus)
*   **Parasympathetic**: Rest & Digest
*   **Nucleus Ambiguus**: Gag, Swallow, Vocalize
*   **Largest autonomic conduit** (65-80% afferent)
### CN XI (Spinal Accessory)
*   **SCM + Trapezius**: Shoulder, Neck
### CN XII (Hypoglossal)
*   **Tongue**: Deviates to weak side
### Medullary Syndromes
*   **Medial**: Tongue ipsilateral, Hemiparesis contralateral
*   **Lateral (PICA)**: Hoarse, Dysphagia, Ipsi ataxia

flashcards.front: CN VII UMN vs LMN lesion?
flashcards.back: UMN: Lower face only. LMN: Entire face (forehead + lower)
Ipsilateral complete facial paralysis, dry eye, hyperacusis
